problems.issue: The stack holes (15.25, 15.25) sit at r = 21.57 mm on the arm diagonals, inside the arm's rounded root (centre r = 31, radius 10, so solid from r = 21.0). The M3 x 30 stack screw (22 mm stack + 5 mm body = 27 mm) sticks out 3 mm below the body bottom straight into the arm top. A probe confirms arm material on the screw axis at z = -0.5 to -2.9 and 15.3 mm^3 of overlap with the screw tip. Arms go on before the stack (DESIGN step 3 before step 5), so the stack screws hit the arm before they clamp. M3 x 25 would only catch about 0.4 mm of the nut. Same on all four arms. The interference check mis
problems.fix: Move the arm root clear of the stack nuts: arm_r0 >= 35 (root edge at r >= 25, beyond the nut pocket at r = 24.9) and re-run the arm FEA. Alternatively, cut a 4 mm dia x 4 mm deep relief in each arm root top at x = 21.57. Separately, the engine should check the protruding screw tip against neighbouring items.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The XT60 cradle closes both ends of the connector. The front end wall (x = -40.35 to -38.45) is solid. The rear end wall (x = -63.55 to -61.95) has only a 6.1 mm slot (|y| < 3.05) for an 8.1 mm wide connector, confirmed by point probes at the cradle mid-height. An XT60 mates along its length, so the battery lead's plug cannot reach the mating face from either end. The solder-cup side is also walled off, so the leads can only leave through the open bottom.
problems.fix: Open the mating end of the cradle fully (no end wall across the 8.1 x 16 face). Hold the connector against unplugging pull with a full-width stop behind its housing shoulder, or with the cable tie plus a rear lip that sits only above or below the housing. Leave the solder-cup end open toward the ESC. Then add a check (insert path or keep-out box) for the mating plug's approach along -x.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Each arm is held against yaw only by two M3 screws in a line along the arm, 14 mm apart, in printed plastic. A side hit on a motor (the most common freestyle crash: a gate, branch or pole) puts about F x 68 / 14 = 4.9 F of bearing load on each screw. That load goes into the 5 mm body hole and nut pocket, with only 2.3 mm of plastic under the nut. Bearing in that hole crushes at roughly 100 N side load. Friction from screws clamped into plastic drops as the PETG creeps. The damage lands in the body, the part that is not meant to be replaceable, instead of in the arm.
problems.fix: Key each arm root into the body: a 1.5-2 mm deep pocket in the body underside shaped like the arm root (or two printed ribs either side), so side loads go into a shoulder and not the screws. If space allows, also spread the screws across the arm (two side by side plus one on the axis) rather than in a line.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Motor screws are M3 x 10 with a 7.0 mm grip, so 3.0 mm goes into the motor. That is exactly the catalog max_screw_depth of 3.0 mm, which is itself only 'typical' (unpublished). There is zero margin for screw length tolerance (ISO 4762 L = 10 is +/-0.29 mm), the printed counterbore floor tolerance, or a slightly shallower flange. A screw touching the stator windings shorts a phase and kills the motor or ESC. Applies to all four arms.
problems.fix: Sink the heads 0.5 mm deeper (counterbore_depth = t - 7.5, so 2.5 mm into the motor, matching iFlight's stock M3 x 8 on 5-6 mm arms), or keep 7 mm and specify M3 x 9. Also make the fastener check reject engagement above max_screw_depth minus a tolerance margin.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The camera is unprotected in a crash. The pivot is at x = 48 and the lens sits 13.9 mm ahead of it, about x = 60-62 depending on tilt. The nose and cheeks end at x = 55, so the lens is the first thing to hit in a frontal crash. The cheeks are 3 x 14 mm walls, 18 mm tall, printed upright with no root fillet. A frontal hit bends them across the layer lines (z strength ~29 MPa, no SF check), right at the body-to-cheek layer seam.
problems.fix: Extend the cheeks (or a separate bumper) at least 3 mm past the lens front over the whole 0-40 deg range. Thicken the cheeks to 4 mm with r >= 2 mm root fillets into the body, or make the camera cage a separate TPU part, as Source One does.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The body has no fea_static requirement, although it carries all four arm moments and is the part the design says must outlive the arms (ENGINEERING.md section 3b: every structural part). Hand checks show it is no better off than the arm. At the inner arm screw (r = 38), the section across the diagonal is about 40 x 5 mm net (Z ~ 167 mm^3), giving about 33 N x 75 mm / 167 = 15 MPa if the body carries the moment alone, against an allowable of 35/3 = 11.7 MPa. Composite action with the arm reduces that, but nothing proves it. The outer arm screw at r = 52 is 5.5 mm from the body corner, below the
problems.fix: Add an fea_static requirement on the body: arm_1 crash moment entering at the arm_1 bolt sites, fixed or balanced at the opposite arm or posts, SF 3. Move arm_hole_2 inward to <= 49, or raise body_half to 46, so the outer screw has >= 6 mm edge distance. The arm should be the weakest link by margin.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: There is no provision for a video transmitter, receiver or antenna mount. The brief's analog 19 mm micro camera is useless without a VTX, and a real build needs a VTX (usually a 20x20 M2 or 30.5 stack layer, 4-6 mm) plus an SMA/U.FL antenna holder at the rear and a receiver and antenna tubes. The space under the top plate cannot take a VTX on the stack: stack top at z = 27, M3 heads to ~30, strap under the plate at ~30.5, plate underside at 32.
problems.fix: Budget a VTX (catalog entry plus proxy) as a stack layer or a 20x20 mount on the top-plate underside, with raised post_h if needed. Props clear the plate by radius, so height costs no prop margin. Add a rear antenna mount (SMA bulkhead or printed antenna tube holder) and a receiver pocket and cable path.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

Magenta over-limit spots show at the outer bolt seat. Either the render is stale or the two come from different runs.
problems.fix: Regenerate the render from the same solve. After the arm_r0 change, re-check the margin; the outer-screw fulcrum load is not modelled (see the body finding).

problems.issue: Flight stiffness and heat are not verified. A hand calc gives the first arm bending mode at about 165 Hz (EI = 2460 x 2218 N mm^2, 36 g tip mass, 75 mm free length), before allowing for clamp compliance. That sits in the gyro noise band. PETG-CF softens around 70-80 C, close to the temperature of a hard-run 2207 motor sitting directly on the pad.
problems.fix: Note it in the build notes (DESIGN already asks for a hover test and Blackbox check). Consider a 1 mm air gap or standoff ring under the motor base, and a stiffer arm section (taller I or rib) if Blackbox shows a resonance around 150 Hz.

problems.issue: The lens is protected front-on but not from above. The cheek tops slope from z = 25 (x <= 56) down to 18 at x = 68 to clear the props. At home tilt (25 deg) the lens centre is at about (60.6, 24.9), and at 40 deg about (58.6, 27.9) plus the barrel radius, while the cheek top there is about 22-23.5. So the upper half of the lens, and at max tilt all of it, stands above the cage. A flat frontal wall hits the cheeks first (good), but a branch, pole or gate edge above about 23 mm hits the lens. In nose-down forward flight the leading edge is the nose bottom, so this mainly matters for climbing hit

problems.issue: The yaw-key ridges (3 x 1.5 mm, 22 mm long, printed on the arm top) take side loads by bending and shear at their root, which is a layer interface. For a 33 N side hit at the motor (lever about 66 mm to the ridge centre), the linear-bearing distribution gives about 13.5 N/mm peak per ridge: bending about 6.8 MPa plus shear about 4.5 MPa at the root, against 29/3 = 9.7 MPa across layers. The margin is thin, and the arm's in-plane strength is not used.
problems.fix: Make the ridges 4 mm wide with a 0.5 mm root fillet, or better, sink the whole arm root 1.5 mm into a body-underside pocket shaped like the arm, so the arm's full 11 mm side faces bear in-plane and the screws stay pure clamp. Either change keeps the arm the replaceable weak link.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: The VTX screw length does not match the hardware. The fastener check sizes M2 x 12 for an 8 mm grip because the TX800 proxy is an 8 mm solid block. The real board is a single PCB (about 1.6 mm) with a heatsink that does not cover the 20 x 20 corner holes, so an M2 x 12 head would sit about 6 mm below the PCB and clamp nothing unless 6 mm spacers are fitted. Spacers are not in the BOM.
problems.fix: Either list 4 x M2 x 6 mm nylon spacers in bom_extra, or keep the 8 mm grip and add the spacers explicitly. Alternatively, size the screw for PCB + washer + boss (M2 x 6 into the 6 mm pilot).
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Wire path: the rear post pair (x = -31.5, y = +/-5, 9 mm dia with a 1 mm gap, z 7-45) stands directly between the XT60 solder cups (x = -40.35, y = 0) and the ESC battery pads at the rear-centre of the ESC (x = -22.8). The 12 AWG power leads, and the usual low-ESR capacitor, must detour about 10 mm sideways around the pair. The antenna/receiver tie slots in the rear tab leave only 1.2 mm of material to the tab edge. There is no real antenna mount (only tie slots), so a crash will load the VTX's MMCX socket. problems.issue: Engine change kerf/electrical.py connector_burst_limit: I judge this a loosened check, not sound engineering. (1) It fits one thermal time constant (tau = 209 s, the bulk heating of connector plus wire) to two long-time ratings (30 A for 4 h, 60 A for 1 min, both stated as '< 60 C rise', so neither is exactly at the limit). It then extrapolates 12 times shorter than the shortest published time, to 194.9 A: 3.25 times the highest rating anyone publishes and 6.5 times the continuous rating. Short-time heating of a contact is set by the small local mass of the contact spot and pin, not the 209 s
problems.fix: Revert the extrapolation, or cap it at a conservative physical bound: never above the adiabatic limit of the contact pair (sourced contact resistance and pin mass), and never below the wire's own rise on the same run. Then make the design pass honestly, using one of: a cited realistic full-throttle burst length for 5-inch freestyle (from Blackbox logs or a published source) as `burst_s`; a real Be

problems.issue: XT60 retention against unplugging is friction only. The tie now wraps under the connector, which is correct, and holds it up. But nothing bears on the housing when the battery plug is pulled rearward through the open end, and the front stops still sit at the solder-cup tips, so the housing seats 5-7 mm inside the walls. In practice a hard-cinched tie usually holds, but it is the weak point when the pack is unplugged.
problems.fix: Add a 1 mm lip at the rear end above the housing's top edge, clear of the 8.1 x 16 mating face, or a tie groove or notch that bears on the housing step. Keep the probe that shows the tie path is clear.

problems.issue: Camera field of view (estimate, Phoenix 2 at 155 deg diagonal on 4:3, roughly 124 x 93 deg). At 0 deg tilt the cheek tips (x 62-68, |y| 10) sit about 58 deg off the lens axis, inside the roughly 62 deg half-width, so they will show at the image sides at low tilt. At 35-40 deg tilt the roof tongue's front corners, (58, +/-12, 45), come about 60 deg off axis toward the top edge and may show in the top corners. At the 25 deg home tilt both are out of view. Protection from above is now partial: the roof stops 4-7 mm behind the lens front.
problems.fix: Check this on the bench with the camera fitted. If the cheeks show, chamfer their inner front edges to about 45 deg. If the roof corners show at max tilt, round the tongue's front corners with a larger radius.

problems.issue: Phase-wire model. The runs are 18 AWG, 175 mm, 'the motor's own leads extended where needed', and the BOM buys 2.1 m of 18 AWG. The XING2's own lead gauge and length are not in the catalog. If they are 20 AWG (common on 2207s), the engine's own 60 K-in-5 s rule would fail on them, since rise scales with 1/A^2, giving about 150 K at 35 A. If they are long enough to reach the ESC (about 110 mm needed), no extension is needed at all. Also, bat_lead is 'the pack's own lead', but its 200 mm is still included in the 0.4 m of 12 AWG to buy.
problems.fix: Add the motor lead gauge and length to the catalog from the iFlight page. Model ph1-4 as the real leads (or keep 18 AWG extensions with solder joints, consistently). Exclude bat_lead from the wire purchase.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: Flight time is reported as 13.08 min at hover, from momentum theory with FM 0.5 and eta 0.75 (93.5 W for 558 g). Thrust tables for 2207/5.1-inch on 6S suggest real hover is nearer 110-140 W, and freestyle is 3-5 min on a 1300 pack. The requirement (>= 3 min) passes either way, but 13 min will mislead Spencer.
problems.fix: Label it 'hover-only, ideal estimate' in WIRING.md and DESIGN, and give a freestyle expectation of 3-5 min, or catalogue the iFlight throttle table and use measured hover current.

problems.issue: The `power` pass depends on a Betaflight setting that the build package never tells Spencer to make. On the mechanism itself: Betaflight `motor_output_limit` is real. It is applied in the mixer to every motor's final output. On the BLHeli_S 55 A ESC there is no firmware current limit at all, so this output cap is the only cap available, and it is the same kind of cap tvc_drone uses (MOT_SPIN_MAX). I accept it as an honest configured cap under ENGINEERING.md 10b, with one condition: it has to actually be configured. Today `set motor_output_limit = 74` appears only in DESIGN.md (assembly step 9)
problems.fix: Engine (general, so tvc_drone gets it too): in wiring_out / ship, print every `electrical.limits` entry with its `why` as a 'Configure before the first flight' section in WIRING.md, plus a numbered final step in ASSEMBLY.md's electrical list (here: Betaflight CLI `set motor_output_limit = 74`, `save`, then check the Blackbox/OSD current peak on the first punch-out). In the WIRING.md Loads table, s

problems.issue: The cap's current estimate is slightly optimistic, and the comment calls it conservative. project.yaml and DESIGN.md say 35.08 x 0.74^3 = 14.22 A is 'on the high side' because motor efficiency rises at part load. The direction is wrong. At 74 % duty the I*R drop shrinks faster than the drive voltage, so loaded rpm falls by less than 26 %. With roughly 60 mOhm of motor + ESC resistance, rpm comes out near 0.756 of full rather than 0.74. Battery current = duty x motor current = 0.74 x 0.756^2 x 35.08, about 14.8 A per motor, so roughly 60-61 A total against the 60 A rating. A full pack (25.2 V a
problems.fix: Correct the wording: the propeller-law current is a central estimate, not an upper bound. Make the first-flight Blackbox/OSD current check the gate (peak <= 60 A on a full pack, else lower the limit by 1-2 %). Optionally catalogue the iFlight throttle table (it lists current at 50/60/75 % throttle) and use the measured 75 % row instead of the scaling law.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: The XT60 pigtail has very little room to turn. The 12 AWG leads (3.6 mm OD, catalog wire.silicone) leave the cradle's front stops at x -44.55 on the centreline (pins stacked in z). They must be at |y| >= 14.3 (pillar half-width 12.5 + wire radius) by the rear pillar face at x -37.5. That is 14.3 mm sideways in 7 mm forward, about a 5 mm centreline bend radius (1.4 x OD), right at the solder cup. The BOM's '20 mm' heat-shrink over that joint would run past x -37.5 into the pillar. The route check passes because its tube model has no bend radius and no stiff joint section. It can be built with f
problems.fix: Either add a build note (solder the leads pre-bent at 90 deg towards -y, use 8-10 mm heat-shrink on the 12 AWG joints, and change the BOM line), or give the turn about 8 more mm: move the XT60 to x -67 with the tab to -80, or narrow the rear pillar's y extent on the lead side.

problems.issue: The single battery strap sits 14.5 mm ahead of the pack's centre (band x 4.5..24.5 on a pack spanning x -41..41), because the VTX takes up x -27.5..0.5 underneath. The rear 55 mm of the pack is held only by the pad's friction and can lift or yaw about the strap in hard manoeuvres and crashes. I probed the strap loop itself and it is now correct (see summary).
problems.fix: Acceptable as is, with the anti-slip pad. If the pack shifts in testing, add a second strap band at x about -36 (the gap between the rear pillar and the tab), or move the VTX 6-8 mm further back so the band can sit closer to x 0.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The antenna head (x -83.5..-72.5, y -16..-5, z 48-68) and its tube bending up past the tab end (z about 43-48 at y -10.5) sit right where the fingers grip the battery's XT60 plug to plug it in and pull it out (plug at x -70..-79, |y| <= 4, z 29-45). The connector_access probe only sweeps the 8.1 x 16 mm connector section, not a hand. Each battery swap will catch the antenna. It is clear of the prop discs: 16.5 mm above prop_3.
problems.fix: Mirror the antenna to the +y side, or move its exit forward of the plug zone (up through a slot at about x -45, y -12), so that y -12..+12 behind the tab is free for fingers.

problems.issue: The 8-10 mm heat-shrink note for the XT60 pigtail is in WIRING.md, ASSEMBLY.md and DESIGN.md, but the generated BOM still lists 'heat-shrink for AWG 12 joints, 20 mm pieces' (row 35). problems.issue: Nothing positively stops the XT60 from pulling out rearward. The front stops take the plugging-in force, but against the 20-40 N it takes to unplug an XT60, only the cable tie's friction holds the male connector (the cradle is open at the rear). Unplugging the battery every flight can walk the connector out of the cradle and load the pigtail's solder joints at the ESC pads.
problems.fix: Add a 0.8-1 mm lip at the cradle's rear edge that clips behind the housing's mating face (the plug only needs the 8.1 x 16 mm opening), or a second tie through slots at x about -66. At the least, add a build note: hold the XT60 body when unplugging.

problems.issue: The generated ASSEMBLY.md never says to drop the 12 M3 nuts into the arm and stack nut pockets, or to tape the stack nuts, whose pockets open downward. It also puts every soldering step after the top plate, battery and strap are on. DESIGN.md has the correct order (nuts in step 2, solder in step 5 before the top plate). The source docstrings are stale: arm.py says the arm screws are M3 x 12 (BOM and fastener check: M3 x 14), and body.py says the post screws are M3 x 6 (BOM: M3 x 8).
problems.fix: Engine: for nut_trap receivers, add a 'press N nuts into <part> pockets' line before the step that drives the screws (and say so when a pocket opens downward). Let a project put the electrical steps before a named mechanical step (here, before top_plate). Fix the two docstrings.

The wiring routes ph1-ph4 along exactly that line, at z 9 between the two ribs (local [24,0,9] -> [64,0,9]). The tip then ends at z 6, 0.3 mm past the nut and 1 mm below the top face. Re-run body_strength, because the inner-nut pull-down is the body's load case. problems.issue: The build documents never call for a thread-locker. The motor screws are steel into the motor's aluminium base and the arm screws use plain M3 nuts, on a vibrating airframe. Motor screws backing out is a classic 5-inch failure.
problems.fix: Add 'blue (medium) thread-locker on the 16 motor screws; nylon-insert or thread-locked nuts on the arm screws' to the build notes and the BOM. Keep thread-locker off the plastic and away from the nylon VTX spacers.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The arm prints top-up, so the M3 counterbores (motor: 3.5 mm deep; arm root: 5 mm) open on the bed face. Each counterbore ceiling is an unsupported 6 mm annulus round the 3.4 mm hole, where the screw head seats. It prints, but it droops unless it is bridged properly.
problems.fix: Turn on the slicer's hole-bridging or sacrificial-layer option, or add a 0.2 mm sacrificial layer at the counterbore ceiling in the part and drill it out. Check that the screw heads seat flat.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The BOM buy links are for the wrong screw lengths. bom.md row 'M3 x 12 mm socket head screw' (8 off, the arm screws) links to Zoro SC22030080, an 'M3 ... 8 mm L, 100 PK'. catalog/prices.json has no 'screw:M3x12:socket', so ship.py falls back to 'screw:M3:socket', which is an M3 x 8 pack (it was an exact M3 x 14 entry in round 6, so the M3 x 12 change caused this). The row 'M2 x 12 mm socket head screw' (4 off, VTX) has the same fault: it links to the M2 x 6 pack SC22020060. The row price is also taken from the wrong pack. An M3 x 8 from below with a 6 mm grip ends at z 2, short of the nut seat

problems.issue: Round-6 major, now resolved. The only remaining exposure: each arm nut now sits at the bottom of an open 1 mm deep hex well (about 5.8 mm across flats) on the phase-wire line, with the thread end 1 mm below the top face and 0.3 mm above the nut. Soft 18 AWG silicone pressed into the well by a tie or a crash could still reach the thread end, but only if it bends to a radius of about 4 mm. That is unlikely.
problems.fix: Optional: after the arms are torqued, put a dab of hot glue or RTV in each of the 8 wells, or a 25 mm strip of Kapton under each phase bundle. Add one line to the build notes.

problems.issue: Thread engagement in the sunk nut is near the minimum. The tip is only 0.3 mm past the nut top. The M3 x 12 length tolerance is +/-0.35 mm (js15) and the tip chamfer is about 0.5 mm, so a short screw fully engages only about 1.8-2.2 mm of the 2.4 mm nut. The thread-stripping strength is still well over 1 kN against the 144 N design load, so this is not a strength problem. But no thread shows past the nut, so a nylon-insert nut cannot be used and the joint relies on threadlocker.
problems.fix: Accept it, and keep the blue threadlocker on these 8. In the build notes, say to check that the screw end is flush with or past the top of the nut.

problems.fix: Power the camera from the stack's 9 V pad (the Phoenix 2 accepts 5-36 V per the catalog, and the BEC is rated 3 A), or use 26 AWG for cam_5v. Either gets rid of the sag row.

problems.issue: FEA is judged on the engine's 99.9th-percentile stress. The body passes at 10.76 MPa against 11.67. The volume peak is 20.7 MPa and the surface peak 15.6 MPa, both above the 11.67 allowable. The hot spot is the rib-to-plate junction at the arm_1 screws, which is where the load goes, but it has little margin if the p99.9 convention hides a real concentration.
problems.fix: Print a spare body and a crash-test arm_1 load coupon, or add 1 mm more rib root fillet / a wider rib foot. Do not lower the 3 SF.

problems.issue: T/W is 6.02 against a 6.0 floor, on a 161 g printed-mass estimate and a 74 % output cap. DESIGN.md says 3 g of extra print mass fails it. The pillars run across the layers at 7.0 / 9.0 MPa against 9.67, so that margin is also thin.
problems.fix: Weigh the printed parts before flying. If heavy, widen the lightening windows in the top plate and body, not the pillars. Keep the 4-wall setting on the pillars.

problems.issue: The 14.22 A per motor at the 74 % limit is a propeller-law estimate, not a firmware limit. BLHeli_S has no current limit, and peak 57.5 A sits against the XT60's 60 A rating. The brief's twr contract assumes catalog thrust x 4, and this project uses a reduced 3691 g.
problems.fix: Keep the Blackbox/OSD punch-out gate as a mandatory first-flight step. Consider an XT90 or an AM32 ESC if the logged peak is above 55 A.

problems.issue: The motor-screw edge-distance warnings (88 % of the ring is material on the arm pad, 46-50 % at the top-plate insert and VTX pilot holes) are forced by the purchased hole patterns. The motor M3 x 10 gives only 2.5 mm thread engagement in a motor whose thread depth is typical, not published, so the 0.5 mm margin to the windings is unverified.
problems.fix: Measure the thread depth of one motor before tightening all 16 screws (already in DESIGN.md risks). Add a note to the top-plate heat-set inserts to be pressed slowly to avoid splitting the 46 % ring.

problems.issue: New since round 9 (engine check added in d3677bb): report.json warns that the bom_extra row 'M2 x 6 mm button head screw' duplicates the fastener check's M2 screws. It is a false positive: the 2 x M2 x 6 button heads are the camera pivots, the 4 x M2 x 12 socket heads are the VTX screws, and the BOM correctly lists both. A builder reading the warning could still drop the camera screws.
problems.fix: Engine: compare length and head type before calling a bom_extra row a duplicate, or let a row carry a 'distinct from group X' reason that silences the warning. No geometry change needed.
